full_judgment:
2. The facts, in short, are that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted a Title Suit being No. 23 of 1994 in the court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Khulna which was transferred to the court of the learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Khulna and was registered and numbered as Title Suit No. 173 of 1994. The suit was for a decree of partition against this petitioners and others on the allegation contending, inter-alia, that the land of C.S. Khatian No. 158 under mouza Madinabad belonged to Sunu Morol and thereafter the said land was recorded in the name of Sunu Morol in R.S. Khatian No. 239 and S.A. Khatian No. 186. For arrears of rent a Certificate Case No. 619 of 1964-65 was started and the land was purchased by Asgor Ali Morol, Abu Bakkar Morol, Zahurul Haque Morol, Abdul Alek Morol, Jabbar Sarder on 26.06.1965 and possession was delivered on 09.03.1966. 

 4. The predecessor of defendant No. 14 who are petitioner Nos. 1-8 and defendant No. 15 who is petitioner No. 9 contested the suit by filing written statement on the allegation contending, inter-alia, that the suit cannot be maintained in the present form and in the manner as described and that there was no cause of action to file the suit by the plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs had no right to file the suit. The case of the defendants is that the father's name of Sunu Morol was Tarif Morol and the name of Sunu Morol was recorded in C.S. Khatian without recording the names of other heirs of Tarif Morol. Their further case is that Tarif Morol died leaving 1 son, Sunu Morol, 4 daughters namely, Khotejan, Nekjan, Shukjan and Deljan but the record was prepared only in the name of Sunu Morol who with an ulterior motive to deprive his sisters from their shares started a certificate case being No. 619/64-65 and through this certificate case Sunu Morol got the land auction purchased in auction in the name of Alek 'Morol, 3 sons of Alek, Morel and one A. Jabbar and that Sunu Morol purchased 1/6th  shares of land from Karim Sardar and Rahim Sardar who were the sons of his sister Nekjan on 16.09.1968. Thereafter, Sunu Morol transferred 4 acres of land to Abdul Jabbar Sardar and A. Latif Sardar on 03.03.1969 and that either Alek Morol or his sons Abu Bakar, Azgor and lahurul did never claim any title in the suit land on the basis of auction purchase and Sunu Morol's 1/3rd shares of his own and 1/6th shares which he purchased from his sister's sons and he became owner in possession of  1⁄2  share. Then he transferred 6.80 acres of land. Shukjan died leaving her son Keramat and 2 daughters i.e. Sabjan and Kad Bibi who transferred their 1/6th shares by way of a registered deed dated 12.09.1968 to the defendant No. 15 and Khodeja also transferred her share by way of registered deed dated 12.09.1968 to defendant No. 14 and in this manner the defendant Nos.14 and 15 have been possessing 4.16 acres of land along with other land having right, title and interest and Khoda Baksh, son of Khodezan and the sister of Sunu Morol sold his share on 12.09.1968 to one Akbar Ali Khan and that the plaintiffs did not possess any land on the basis of auction purchase. The defendant Nos.14 and 15 and Abdul Jabbar were facing difficulties in managing and possessing their 4.16+2.00=6.16 acres of land due to the disturbance crested by the plaintiffs for which the defeddant No. 14 filed a C.R. Case being No.  119 of 1988 in the court of the Magistrate at Koira and it was ultimately decided in favour of the defendant with regard to their possession of the land. The plaintiffs being aggrieved filed a Criminal Revision No. 244 of 1989 before the learned Sessions Judge, Khulna who after hearing affirmed the order of the learned Magistrate and that the alleged mutation in the names of the plaintiffs and subsequent correction of the record were collusive and fraudulent and that the plaintiffs did no possess 5.7320 acres of land as auction purchasers and .59 acres of land as the heirs of Alek Morol. But the defendants did not file any cash in order to set aside the auction purchase. 

 8. It appears that in the instant suit the sale certificate exhibit-2 was admitted into evidence without any objection and the High Court Division rightly held the same to be genuine one. It further appears that the High Court Division considered C.S. khatian and the mutated khatian in favour of the plaintiff and tightly decreed the suit.
